forces.title: National HealthTech Access Programme drives diagnostic tool uptake
forces.description: The National HealthTech Access Programme (NHAP) is designed to support the uptake of high-impact medical technologies. This includes specific mention of 'AI tools for prostate and breast cancer,' which directly benefit diagnostic service providers. The programme aims for low-friction procurement and value-based purchasing, streamlining the adoption of innovative diagnostic solutions and improving patient access, thereby driving demand and efficiency for Labs & Diagnostics providers in the UK.
forces.source_title: Life Sciences Sector Plan: One Year On

forces.title: Health Data Research Service and improved data access
forces.description: The establishment of the Health Data Research Service (HDRS) and ongoing policy/legislative reforms for data access and governance aim to enable secure, efficient access to health data for research and innovation. For Labs & Diagnostics, which generate and rely heavily on data, this represents a structural shift toward a more connected R&D system. It facilitates advanced analytics, better diagnostic insights, and participation in research, fostering innovation and potentially creating new service offerings.
forces.source_title: Life Sciences Sector Plan: One Year On

forces.title: Scaling up NHS Genomic Medicine Service and testing
forces.description: The NHS Genomic Medicine Service continues to scale, having delivered over 850,000 genomics tests and sequenced more than 45,000 whole genomes in the first six months of 2025/26. This ongoing expansion represents a significant and direct tailwind for Labs & Diagnostics specializing in genomic testing. It drives increased demand for these advanced diagnostic services, solidifying the UK's position as a leader in genomic medicine and powering research and innovation within diagnostic labs.
forces.source_title: Life Sciences Sector Plan: One Year On

forces.title: Reduced clinical trial setup times boosts diagnostic involvement
forces.description: Clinical trial setup times in the UK have significantly decreased from 169 days to 122 days in the first half of 2025/26. This acceleration of research timelines, along with an expansion of Commercial Research Delivery Centres (21 hospital-based, 14 primary care), indirectly benefits Labs & Diagnostics. Faster and more frequent trials create increased opportunities for diagnostic service providers to participate, offering essential testing and analysis, thereby supporting growth and engagement in the broader life sciences R&D ecosystem.
forces.source_title: Life Sciences Sector Plan: One Year On

forces.title: AI adoption in healthcare drives productivity, redefines roles
forces.description: Healthcare organizations, including diagnostic labs, are facing an opportunity to redesign operating models through AI and automation. While AI is expected to lift UK labor productivity by 3.4% over the next decade, it may also lead to a moderately negative employment effect (-1.1%). For Labs & Diagnostics, this means potential for significant productivity gains in administrative functions, data management, scheduling, and potentially diagnostic interpretation, but also a need to re-skill workforces and redesign roles for human-AI collaboration.
forces.source_title: The real future of work in healthcare

viewpoints.title: UK Life Sciences Sector on track to be Europe's leader by 2030
viewpoints.description: The UK government reports strong progress in its Life Sciences Sector Plan, aiming to be the leading life sciences economy in Europe by 2030 and third globally by 2035. Key indicators like R&D investment, access to scale-up capital, and FDI show robust performance, creating a favourable environment for all sub-sectors, including Labs & Diagnostics. Faster clinical trial setups and HealthTech access initiatives further underpin this positive outlook, signaling sustained government commitment to innovation and growth across the healthcare ecosystem.
viewpoints.source_firm: gov.uk (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)
viewpoints.source_title: Life Sciences Sector Plan: One Year On

demand_drivers.driver: Increasing clinical integration of genomic testing
demand_drivers.description: The NHS Genomic Medicine Service is actively scaling up, indicating a growing demand for and integration of genomic diagnostics into standard clinical practice, driving volume for Labs & Diagnostics.
Government commitment and investment, such as the £600 million joint funding for the Health Data Research Service, underpin the expansion of genomic capabilities and related diagnostic services.

market_sizing.methodology: The NHS Genomic Medicine Service delivered over 850,000 genomics tests and sequenced over 45,000 whole genomes in the first six months of the 2025/26 fiscal year. This figure represents the volume of activity for a significant advanced diagnostic service within the UK healthcare system, showcasing the scale of genomic testing being performed by diagnostic labs.
